tasks.short: Consult specialists and prepare appropriate referrals

steps.what: Assess whether conditions exceed scope and identify appropriate specialists
Prepare referral letter from verified findings and consultation question

loop.purpose: Draft a referral without adding clinical facts
loop.input: Verified referral notes and named consultation question
loop.check: Practitioner compares question, urgency, findings, negatives and uncertainty with notes
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved omissions require manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative synthesis varies; fixed fields alone do not express the clinical question

steps.what: Consult with specialists or check and send the referral

tasks.design: Use the clinical record {OTHER} to draft referral text from practitioner-verified notes, with a bounded model loop only for narrative assembly. The practitioner decides whom to consult, checks the exact letter and sends it or conducts the consultation; urgent contact keeps its existing route.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting a clinical question and relevant history takes time even after the referral decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from a restricted note set can reduce rewriting while retaining a clinical check.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising scope limits, urgency and the right specialist, then agreeing responsibility.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner can challenge an uncertain interpretation and negotiate a safe handover.
tasks.altitude: Less referral rewriting, with consultation and referral authority unchanged.

reach.task: Review the specific uncertainty in a specialist referral
reach.learn: Concise clinical questions and explicit urgency

evidence.claim: Juvoly drafts referral letters; the digest establishes capability, not a saving for this practitioner workflow.
Restricted-note drafting with retained consultation time may reduce rewriting; allocations are scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is practitioner referral preparation and contact, excluding specialist labour and full encounter recording. Consultation-only cases bypass letter drafting.

Practitioner produces patient identifier, destination, clinical question, urgency, findings, medications, uncertainty and source references in s1; its full 40 hours include selection and capture. Missing fields are queried manually, never inferred.
The clinical record is {OTHER}. Test native referral templates before adding a loop; existing letter generation earns no new saving. No ready transcript is assumed.
s3 checks the final letter and patient/destination before release. A change invalidates approval; local professional scope determines who may refer.
Referral documentation must not also be counted as a gain in general record maintenance.
unknowns: Current referral templates and writing burden
research_questions: Does source-restricted drafting reduce total capture, editing and release time without losing referral uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Clinical decision and verified source capture
Narrative checks and manual draft corrections
Final letter check, release and consultation

incremental.description: Maintain templates and audit referral omissions

approvals.approved_version: Final letter version with patient, destination, urgency, question and attachments; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=40+11+40=91; gross 9 minus 3 upkeep gives net 6. High needs repeated narrative rewriting; low assumes only 3 hours removed, consumed by upkeep. Consultation and clinical decision time retain all hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep current through literature and professional exchange

steps.what: Locate current literature and select relevant developments in nursing
Read literature and assess its relevance to nursing practice
Talk with colleagues and participate in professional organizations or conferences

tasks.design: Configure publication alerts and saved searches in {DOCS}, retaining direct access to full sources. The practitioner selects, reads and critiques the literature and continues professional exchange; alerts do not become clinical advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly locating new publications consumes a small part of learning time.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and source-date filters can reduce repeated retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing study quality and applicability and learning from colleagues' experience.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner connects evidence with difficult real cases and challenges weak conclusions.
tasks.altitude: Less source hunting with reading and professional participation intact.

reach.task: Discuss applicability of a new study to local practice

evidence.claim: Saved searches can shorten retrieval while full reading and critical appraisal remain; this is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers professional learning, not adopting or publishing a new clinical policy.
Practitioner creates search topics, source selection, date limits and inclusion choices within retained s1 time of 12 hours. No structured relevance label is supplied free.
Native source alerts and search are tried first. Missing full texts or noisy alerts require manual searching in retained time; current alert use earns no new saving.
Colleague and conference time is unchanged; no attendance or learning is replaced by a summary.
unknowns: Existing alert use and retrieval burden
research_questions: Do saved searches shorten retrieval while preserving relevant contrary evidence?

already_counted.description: Search formulation, source checks and alert triage

incremental.description: Maintain search topics and source access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=12+50+30=92; gross 8 minus 2 upkeep gives net 6. High assumes repeated manual retrieval; low assumes only 2 hours removed, offset by upkeep. Reading and exchange retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine follow-up interval and visit requirements to monitor patients
Locate available follow-up visits matching clinical and patient requirements
Schedule the agreed follow-up visit and explain attendance arrangements

tasks.design: Configure clinical scheduling {OTHER} to filter available visits against practitioner-entered requirements. The practitioner confirms suitability, resolves access barriers and books the agreed visit with the patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding a slot can require repeated availability checks against several constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Native appointment filters can expose matching options without deciding clinical follow-up.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the interval, handling deterioration and finding an acceptable option when capacity is scarce.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner can recognise that a routine slot would be unsafe or impractical.
tasks.altitude: Less slot hunting; clinical timing and patient agreement remain personal.

reach.task: Resolve attendance barriers for an agreed appointment

evidence.claim: Native appointment filters can reduce repeated availability checks without selecting clinical timing; the saving is modelled.

assumptions: Boundary is practitioner scheduling time, not patient time, treatment monitoring or administrative staff labour.

Practitioner produces patient identifier, earliest/latest clinically acceptable date, visit type, duration, clinician requirement and accessibility constraints in s1; its 30 hours retain all judgement and field capture.

Scheduling staff maintain appointment identifier, start, duration, visit type, clinician and availability through the existing rota process; their unchanged capture labour is outside this role and earns no saving. s2 checks live availability and missing fields manually within 28 retained hours.
Use native filters before custom matching. Existing runtime earns no saving. Conflicts, clinical change or unavailable options return to manual coordination; nothing is auto-booked.
unknowns: Clinical scheduling fields and native filters
research_questions: Can filters reduce search and rework without delaying clinically required follow-up?

already_counted.description: Availability checks and manual exception coordination

incremental.description: Maintain matching fields and investigate scheduling mismatches

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=30+28+30=88; gross 12 minus 2 upkeep gives net 10. High needs repeated multi-constraint searching; low assumes only 2 hours removed by filters, offset by upkeep. Clinical and patient discussion time is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain departmental safety and infection-control procedures

steps.what: Review current policies, safety findings and infection control requirements
Maintain departmental policies and procedures in the controlled document format
Consult colleagues and resolve policy changes through departmental approval

tasks.design: Use controlled templates and native version comparison in {DOCS} to reduce formatting and revision assembly. The practitioner still assesses safety meaning, resolves changes with colleagues and submits the exact package through existing departmental approval; publication is outside this boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Revision assembly and repeated formatting obscure the substantive policy work.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled templates and comparisons can reduce assembly without writing safety instructions automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether guidance fits local clinical practice and gaining agreement on a safe change.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner can identify operational consequences that a document comparison cannot judge.
tasks.altitude: Less revision assembly; safety judgement and departmental authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check whether an infection-control revision can be applied in practice

evidence.claim: Native controlled templates and version comparisons can reduce assembly work while substantive safety decisions remain manual; time allocations are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is practitioner contribution to policy maintenance, excluding final departmental authorisation, publication and frontline execution.

Practitioner produces source identifier, version, section, proposed change, rationale and local impact in s1, with all 40 hours retained. s2 includes entry, formatting checks and manual text editing within 20 retained hours; no pre-approved safety text is assumed.
s3 produces a submission, not permission to publish. The policy owner uses the existing approval route outside this task; no transferred work or reduction is claimed.
Try native templates and comparison first; current functionality earns no gain. Missing versions or ambiguous changes return to manual reconstruction.
unknowns: Actual assembly burden and document controls
research_questions: Do templates reduce revision assembly without hiding clinically meaningful changes?

already_counted.description: Revision entry, manual editing and formatting checks

incremental.description: Maintain templates and check revision-control integrity

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=40+20+35=95; gross 5 minus 2 upkeep gives net 3. High assumes repeated formatting work; low removes only 2 hours and spends them on upkeep. Clinical review and consultation keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce referral rewriting, reference hunting and scheduling searches while retaining clinical decisions and professional discussion.
reach: Work with specialists on clear referral questions and clinical nurse specialists on source-traceable policy changes
role.ambitious_version: A practitioner who provides clear handovers and accessible follow-up while keeping clinical judgement and local approval responsibilities explicit.
